mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 6% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 shows year-over-year decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) both rise simultaneously for two consecutive months, it signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both increase for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS jumps >0.5% MoM and UNRATE is stable.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) for six consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related earnings and confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during six-month HOUST up-trends.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) both rise together for three consecutive months, it signals a coordinated expansion in household demand, which lifts corporate revenues and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 and HOUST both rise for three consecutive months.
